text: NexusFlow offers three subscription tiers: Starter ($29/mo, 5 seats, 10 GB storage), Professional ($99/mo, 25 seats, 100 GB storage, SSO), and Enterprise (custom pricing, unlimited seats, SLA 99.99%, dedicated support, SAML/SCIM provisioning). Annual billing grants a 20% discount across all plans. Seats are user-level; service accounts do not consume seat quota.

The NexusFlow API enforces rate limits per API key: 1 000 req/min on Starter, 5 000 req/min on Professional, and 20 000 req/min on Enterprise. Burst allowance is 2× the sustained rate for up to 10 seconds. Exceeding limits returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Rate limit counters reset on a sliding 60-second window, not a fixed minute boundary.

NexusFlow supports webhook delivery with at-least-once semantics. Payloads are signed via HMAC-SHA256; the signature is in the X-NexusFlow-Signature-256 header. Retry policy: exponential backoff up to 5 attempts over 24 hours. A webhook endpoint must respond with 2xx within 10 seconds or the delivery is marked failed. Failed deliveries can be replayed from the dashboard up to 72 hours after the original event.

NexusFlow Workflows support conditional branching, parallel execution, and loop nodes. Maximum workflow depth is 50 nodes. Execution timeout is 15 minutes per run. Each step can emit structured output consumed by downstream steps via JSONPath selectors. Workflow state is persisted in durable storage; a node failure triggers automatic retry with configurable backoff (default: 3 retries, 5 s initial delay, factor 2).

Data residency options: US (us-east-1, us-west-2), EU (eu-central-1, eu-west-1), and APAC (ap-southeast-1). Enterprise plans can pin all data to a single region. Cross-region replication for disaster recovery is opt-in and adds 15% to base cost. GDPR data processing agreements (DPA) are available for EU customers via the compliance portal.

NexusFlow AI Assistant (beta) uses a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. It has read-only access to your workspace data via scoped API tokens. No workspace data is used to train foundation models. Retention of AI conversation logs: 30 days, configurable to 0 for zero-retention mode. AI features are disabled by default on accounts with HIPAA BAA addenda.

Remote work policy (effective 2024-Q1): Employees may work remotely up to 4 days per week. Core collaboration hours are 10:00–15:00 local time, Monday–Thursday. All remote employees must maintain a stable broadband connection (min 50 Mbps down) and use a company-approved VPN when accessing internal systems. Home office equipment stipend: $800 one-time, $200/year recurring.

PTO accrual schedule: 0–2 years tenure → 15 days/year; 2–5 years → 20 days/year; 5+ years → 25 days/year. Unused PTO carries over up to 40 days. Payout on termination is capped at 20 days regardless of accrued balance. PTO requests must be submitted at least 2 weeks in advance for blocks ≥ 5 days. Sick leave is separate: 10 days/year, non-carry-over, non-payable on exit.

Code of conduct — conflict of interest: Employees must disclose any financial interest exceeding 1% equity in a competitor, vendor, or customer. Immediate family employment at such entities also requires disclosure. Disclosures are submitted via the Ethics Portal and reviewed by the Legal & Compliance team within 10 business days. Failure to disclose is grounds for termination.

Performance review cycle: bi-annual (June and December). Ratings: Exceeds, Meets, Partially Meets, Does Not Meet. Managers submit calibrated ratings via Lattice. Merit increase budget is allocated at Exceeds (8–12%) and Meets (3–5%). Employees on a PIP (Performance Improvement Plan) are ineligible for merit increases until two consecutive Meets or above ratings post-PIP completion.

Parental leave: primary caregiver — 16 weeks fully paid, extendable to 24 weeks unpaid. Secondary caregiver — 6 weeks fully paid. Adoption and surrogacy are treated identically. Leave must commence within 12 months of birth/adoption. Benefits (health, dental, vision, 401k employer match) continue throughout the leave period.

ADR-012: Adopt Kafka as the primary event backbone (supersedes Redis Pub/Sub). Rationale: Redis Pub/Sub drops messages when consumers are offline; Kafka's durable log enables replay, fan-out, and independent consumer lag. Decision: Migrate all inter-service events to Kafka topics with 7-day retention. Rejected alternative: RabbitMQ — AMQP overhead unsuitable for high-throughput telemetry. Owner: Platform Engineering. Status: Accepted (2024-04-02).

Database sharding strategy for the Accounts service: Range-based sharding on account_id (UUID v7, lexicographically sortable). 16 logical shards mapped to 4 physical Postgres clusters (4 shards/cluster). Resharding triggers at 80% capacity per cluster; automated via the shard-manager service. Cross-shard queries (< 2% of traffic) route through a scatter-gather aggregator. No distributed transactions — eventual consistency via Outbox pattern.

Runbook: Kafka consumer lag alert (P2). Trigger: consumer group lag > 50 000 messages for > 5 minutes. Step 1 — Check consumer health: kubectl get pods -n kafka-consumers. Step 2 — Inspect lag per partition: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group <group>. Step 3 — If single partition hot: trigger manual partition reassignment. Step 4 — If OOM crash loop: increase JVM heap via helm upgrade, set -Xmx to 2 g. Escalate to on-call lead if lag > 500 000 or SLA breach imminent.

Auth service token lifecycle: Access token TTL = 15 minutes (JWT, RS256, 2048-bit key). Refresh token TTL = 30 days, stored as opaque token in Redis with HSET. Refresh token rotation on every use — old token invalidated immediately. Refresh token reuse detection: if stale token presented, entire token family is revoked (family stored as linked list in Redis). Key rotation schedule: signing keys rotated every 90 days via AWS KMS; old keys retained for 1 hour to drain in-flight tokens.

CDN caching strategy for the API layer: CloudFront sits in front of API Gateway for GET endpoints only. Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 for read-heavy list endpoints. Cache invalidation via CloudFront invalidation API on write operations (P99 < 200 ms). Vary header set on Accept-Language and Authorization to prevent cross-tenant cache poisoning. Cache key includes: path + query string (sorted) + plan tier (injected by Lambda@Edge). Authenticated endpoints: Cache-Control: private, no-store — never cached at CDN.

Service mesh migration to Istio (Phase 2 complete). All inter-service traffic is mTLS by default; plaintext rejected at sidecar. Circuit breaker config per service: outlierDetection with consecutive5xxErrors=5, interval=10s, baseEjectionTime=30s, maxEjectionPercent=50. Traffic splitting for canary deploys via VirtualService weight routing. Observability: traces exported to Jaeger via OpenTelemetry collector. Known issue: Envoy adds ~2 ms p99 latency; acceptable per SLA.

CI/CD pipeline contract: all PRs must pass gate checks before merge. Gates: (1) lint + type-check < 3 min, (2) unit tests ≥ 80% coverage, (3) integration tests against ephemeral DB, (4) SAST via Semgrep, (5) SCA via Snyk — block on CVSS ≥ 7.0. Deploy to staging: auto on merge to main. Promote to production: manual approval from 2 engineers + on-call SRE. Rollback: helm rollback <release> — target < 2 min MTTR for hotfixes.

Issue: Customer reports webhook deliveries failing with no retries. Root cause: Endpoint returned HTTP 200 but body was not JSON — NexusFlow's webhook validator rejected it as malformed and did not retry (retry only triggers on 5xx or network timeout, not parse errors). Resolution: Updated webhook docs to clarify response body is ignored; validator changed to accept any 2xx regardless of body. Deployed in v3.2.1. Workaround provided: return empty 200 response immediately.

Issue: SSO login loop — user redirected repeatedly without landing on dashboard. Root cause: SAML response NameID format mismatch. Customer's IdP (Okta) sent urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress but NexusFlow expected urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent. Resolution: Added NameID format negotiation in SP metadata; both formats now accepted. Customer action: re-export SP metadata from NexusFlow and re-upload to Okta.

Issue: Bulk import of 50 000 records via REST API timing out at ~30 000 records. Root cause: Default API gateway timeout is 29 seconds; bulk sync exceeds this. Resolution: Migrate to async batch import endpoint (/v2/imports) which returns a job_id immediately and processes asynchronously. Poll /v2/imports/{job_id} for status. Completion webhook fires on done/failed. Max batch size per job: 100 000 records.

Issue: Workflow executions silently skipping the 'send email' step. Root cause: SMTP integration credentials expired; the step was configured to fail silently (continue_on_error: true) — a legacy default now changed to false. Resolution: Audit all workflows with continue_on_error; surface credential errors as workflow warnings in the audit log. Customer action: rotate SMTP credentials and set alerting on step failures.

Issue: Dashboard reports show data 2–4 hours stale during peak traffic. Root cause: Read replicas lag due to WAL shipping delay under heavy write load. Reports query was incorrectly routed to replica instead of primary. Resolution: Added query hint to force primary routing for time-sensitive report queries. Long-term fix: promote to logical replication with streaming replication target lag < 5 s. ETA: Q1 2025.

Issue: SCIM provisioning not deprovisioning users when removed from Okta group. Root cause: NexusFlow SCIM handler only processed PATCH /Groups for member adds, not member removals (operations array with op:remove not handled). Resolution: Patched SCIM handler to process all op types; deprovision sets user active=false and revokes all sessions within 60 seconds. Security note: gap existed for up to 2 hours before session expiry on affected tenants.

Competitive analysis: Competitor X launched a native Slack integration in Q3 2024. Key differentiator: two-way sync — actions taken in Slack reflect in Competitor X dashboard in real time. Our current Slack integration is outbound-only (notifications). Customer sentiment analysis (50 interviews): 34% cited Slack bi-directionality as a top-3 missing feature. Recommended priority: P1 for H1 2025 roadmap.

LLM evaluation memo (internal, Q4 2024): Evaluated GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro for the AI Assistant feature. Benchmarks: latency (TTFT), accuracy on domain-specific QA, hallucination rate on structured data. Results: Claude 3.5 Sonnet had lowest hallucination rate (4.2%) on internal product docs. GPT-4o had best TTFT (median 320 ms). Gemini 1.5 Pro had highest throughput for long-context tasks. Decision: Claude 3.5 Sonnet as primary, GPT-4o as fallback for latency-sensitive paths.

Infrastructure cost optimisation memo (2024-Q3): Current monthly AWS spend: $142K. Top 3 cost drivers: RDS ($38K), EKS node groups ($44K), CloudFront ($21K). Identified savings: (1) Switch RDS Aurora Serverless v1 → v2: -$12K/mo; (2) Spot instances for non-critical worker nodes: -$18K/mo estimated; (3) S3 Intelligent-Tiering for assets > 90 days old: -$4K/mo. Total projected savings: ~$34K/mo (~24%). Implementation risk: medium for EKS spot migration.

User research summary — onboarding funnel (N=500 new sign-ups, Aug 2024): D1 activation rate (completed first workflow): 38%. Drop-off analysis: 61% of non-activating users abandoned at the 'Connect Integration' step. Qualitative finding: OAuth permission screen perceived as 'asking for too much access'. Recommendation: Introduce incremental permission prompting (request only read scope initially). Expected lift: +15% D1 activation based on A/B test prototype results.

Security posture review (annual, 2024): Penetration test findings: 2 Critical (both patched), 5 High, 11 Medium. Critical findings: (1) IDOR on /api/v1/reports/{id} — missing tenant ownership check; (2) Stored XSS in workflow name field — insufficient output encoding. Both deployed patches within 48 hours of disclosure. SOC 2 Type II audit: passed with 0 exceptions. ISO 27001 certification target: Q2 2025. Bug bounty program launched on HackerOne.

Vector database evaluation (for AI feature RAG pipeline, Q4 2024): Candidates: Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector. Benchmark: 1M 1536-dim vectors, top-10 ANN search, recall@10, p99 latency. Results: Qdrant — 98.2% recall, 12 ms p99, $0.08/hr managed. Pinecone — 97.8% recall, 18 ms p99, $0.096/hr. pgvector — 95.1% recall, 34 ms p99, marginal add-on cost. Decision: Qdrant (managed cloud) for production; pgvector as fallback for small tenants to reduce ops overhead.
